subject: Nexus pilot: savings roadmap + runtime acceptance checklist
messages:
From: Sam Lee <sam@brightline.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nexus pilot ask — pricing + runbook

Tessa —

Thanks for walking us through Redwood last week. We want to run a short pilot (3 weeks) to validate runtime economics and output quality for our chat summarization workflow. A few asks so we can align internally: 

- Target workload: ~120–180 QPS (burst to 250) on 4k context, expected ~1.2M tokens/day.
- Acceptance criteria: 95th pctl latency <200ms on user-facing route, coherent summary quality per our eval set (we can share), and no PII leakage on customer subset.
- Pricing question: can you propose a pilot credit package + overage rates and one recommended commercial pathway if we move to Reserved/Dedicated?
- Technical: we are interested in quantization and cache guidance — will 4-bit quantization be safe for our summaries? How should we think about KV prefix caching and batching defaults?

I attached our pilot SOW (see Nexus_Pilot_SOW.pdf). Procurement loop (procurement@brightline.ai) is copied for timing. Ideally we sign / start first half of July.

Appreciate a concise plan and any constraints.

— Sam
Sam Lee
Head of Platform, Brightline AI
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Nexus pilot ask — pricing + runbook

Connor, Karthik — forwarding Brightline's asks. Key trade-offs: they want a short pilot but high QPS and tight P95. Can we put a concise offer together (pilot credit + overage, recommended quantization/kv cache/batching defaults) and a short acceptance checklist that legal/procurement can sign off on?

Quick preferences: I think a conservative path is: 4-bit quant with automatic fallback to 8-bit on edge cases, a 30–45% pilot credit on overage, and a short runtime SLA for the pilot (best-effort p95 target + operational guardrails). But I want your technical call on latency/throughput assumptions and an ops-friendly econ.

I'll draft the external note once we have numbers. Can you do bullets by EOD?

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nexus pilot ask — pricing + runbook

Tessa / Karthik —

Quick technical write-up (bullets):

- Quantization: recommend Q4-bit (QLoRA-style) for the pilot to hit cost/latency targets. For summarization workloads we see minimal quality regression vs FP16 for top-k/top-p sampling when combined with light post-filtering. Include an auto-fallback to Q8 path for any eval-set regressions (we can gate by prompt family).

- KV cache: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompt and common context. Suggest TTL = 10m for session-level cache, with automatic cold-start prefetch for expected high-frequency prefixes. This reduces token cost ~20–35% in our benchmarks for similar chat workloads.

- Batching: target continuous batching with max-batch-size tuned to keep p95 <200ms. For their QPS band (120–180): set batch boundary at ~64 concurrent requests and dynamic shaping; expected avg tokens/sec per GPU ~12–15k after q4. If they need tighter p95, reduce batch target and add more dedicated capacity (see ops note).

- Acceptance checklist (draft):
  1) Baseline eval run: run 500 eval prompts from Brightline; target mean ROUGE-L >= baseline provided.
  2) Latency validation: 95th <=200ms on 1-hour steady-state at 150 QPS.
  3) KV cache hit rate >=35% on sample trace.
  4) No PII leaks on sampled traces per their masked test set.

- Pilot credits recommendation: include 250k token credit (covers ~2 days at 150 QPS typical usage) + 45% discount on overage for pilot period. If they convert to a 12-month reserved commit within 30 days, convert pilot credits into an initial commit credit and give an additional 8% commercial discount.

I'll attach a checklist spreadsheet and a short runbook (pilot_acceptance_checklist.xlsx).

Connor
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 Jul 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Nexus pilot ask — pricing + runbook

Adding ops/commercial constraints: 

- GPU sizing: for 150 QPS steady-state with q4 models, plan for a 6–8 GPU pool (A100e-class equivalent) with autoscale headroom for bursts. We can propose a temporary Dedicated burst pool for the pilot to keep performance predictable.

- Commercial: if Brightline is open to a 12-month banded commit (tiered bands), we can structure year-one with a blended 20% discount on base usage + an extra 10% rebate if they hit the top band by Q4. For pilots that convert inside 30 days, as Connor suggested, pilot credits become initial committed credit.

- Legal/Procurement: procurement will likely ask for a short SOW + acceptance checklist. Recommend we provide a one‑page summary for procurement and a detailed tech annex for engineering.

I'll flag potential capacity windows (late July) if they want Dedicated start July 15 — need ops sign-off ASAP.

Karthik
Head of Inference Optimization, Redwood Inference

Subject: Nexus pilot offer + mutual action plan

Sam / Brightline procurement —

Thanks again — below is a concise pilot offer and the mutual action plan so we can get you started quickly. If this looks good I'll queue a DocuSign for the SOW and schedule a 30-minute ops handshake with our infra team.

Offer (pilot, 3 weeks):
- Pilot credits: 250,000 token credit applied to pilot term.
- Pilot overage: 45% discount off list hosted rates for the pilot period.
- Technical profile: Q4-bit quantized model with Q8 fallback guardrails; KV prefix caching (TTL 10m) and continuous batching tuned for p95 <=200ms at 150 QPS.
- Ops: optionally deploy temporary Dedicated burst pool (6 GPUs) for the pilot to stabilize p95 — we will price this separately if you choose to turn on Dedicated.

Commercial pathway if you convert to Reserved within 30 days of pilot end:
- Pilot credits convert to initial committed credit.
- Additional 8% on-top discount on base rates for a 12-month reservation; aggregate year-one structure can be blended into tiered bands (we propose a 3-band commit).

Mutual action plan (high level):
1) This week: confirm SOW and signature (DocuSign link below).
2) Week 1: engineering handshake + baseline eval (we run 500 eval prompts).
3) Week 2: steady-state performance run (target 150 QPS; we validate p95 and KV hit rate).
4) Week 3: review results and decide conversion path.

Attachments: Nexus_Pilot_SOW.pdf, pilot_acceptance_checklist.xlsx, redwood_pricing_summary.xlsx

Next steps: If procurement signs the SOW we can stand up the pilot as early as July 15 (ops capacity permitting). Can we lock a 30-minute slot for July 6–8 for the tech handshake?
